openItems: Paint by Number: the selected number drawn on the page is system blue and the other numbers are 40% grey (`PageView.swift`), and the shapes still waiting for the selected number are tinted light blue (`CanvasRenderer.hint`, 0xCFE6FF). Neither belongs to the Rihla palette yet; palm green or date gold are the natural replacements.

Small springs are not gated on Reduce Motion: the swatch select scale, the route stop size change, the "Try number" bubble slide, the celebration overlay scale-in, and the press scales on cards and buttons. The two large moves (mode slide, seal drop) are gated.

Dark appearance: palm green on the dark sage ground is about 2.1:1. It matters only where green is a line or icon on the ground (the selected brush tile outline, the placeholder icon for a missing thumbnail).
The parental gate is the stock system sheet on purpose; its person icon and bordered answer buttons take the app tint (rail green) from the environment.

narrative.northStar: Rihla, one caravan route across the Kingdom
narrative.overview:
Saudi Colors is a trip with nine stops. The whole app speaks one Saudi design language, chosen by the owner for every region alike: a deep palm green shell, a dotted date-gold caravan route with gold stops, and a calm sage-white ground behind the pages. Regions do not get their own palettes or ornaments. Their character lives in their pictures and their names, in English and Arabic; the chrome around them stays the same so that moving from Najd to Jazan feels like travel through one country, not a jump between apps.

The system has exactly one ornament: a strip of Al-Sadu weaving (red ground, black teeth, a chain of cream and gold diamonds), drawn in code so it stays sharp at any size. It sits where a woven edge would sit: along the bottom of every green header, along the top of the colour tray, at the foot of the celebration card, and as a thin selvedge on each region cover in the rail. Progress is told without reading: eight diamonds per region, gold stops that earn a star when a region is complete, and a green seal with a gold stitched ring pressed onto each finished page.

This is a native iPadOS / iOS 17+ SwiftUI app, iPad-first in landscape, used by children aged 4 to 9 who often cannot read. Density is low and targets are large (60pt minimum). Every child control pairs an SF Symbol with a short label. Display type is SF Rounded at heavy weight; everything else uses the system text styles so Dynamic Type and Arabic shaping come for free. The illustrated scene is always the hero: chrome frames it, the tray sits on plain paper so paint reads true, and nothing decorative is laid over the artwork. Grown-up surfaces (the parental gate) deliberately stay in the stock system sheet style, quiet and separate from play.
keyCharacteristics: One unified Saudi look for all nine regions; variety comes from the scene art.
Deep green rail with a dotted gold route and gold stops (the journey).
Palm green header bands on a sage-white ground.
One ornament only: the Al-Sadu woven band.
Green seal with a gold stitched ring for finished pages.
SF Rounded heavy for display, system text styles elsewhere.
60pt minimum child targets, icon plus label, RTL safe, Reduce Motion honoured on the large moves.

rules.name: The One Saudi Look Rule
rules.body: Every region uses the same palette and the same ornament. Never introduce a per-region colour, header tint or pattern; a region's identity comes from its scene art and its names.

rules.name: The One Green Bar Rule
rules.body: Palm green and rail green carry the same value in light and dark appearance on purpose. Their navigation bars are forced into the dark appearance (`toolbarColorScheme(.dark)`), so a separate dark-mode value would make the bar and the header band below it two different greens. Only the ground, the ink and the gold shift for dark mode.

rules.name: The Paper Tray Rule
rules.body: Anything the child picks paint from (colour tray, number tray, brush sizes) sits on plain system background, never on green or sage, so the swatches look like the paint they will lay down.

rules.name: The Rounded Is For Children Rule
rules.body: SF Rounded is used for text a child reads as a sign or a button. Text that grown-ups read (the parental gate, system dialogs) stays in the standard design.

rules.name: The Text Style Rule
rules.body: Outside the display sizes, use system text styles (`.title2`, `.title3`, `.headline`, `.subheadline`) with a weight, never fixed point sizes, so Dynamic Type works. The region display size is a `@ScaledMetric` tied to largeTitle.

rules.name: The Earned Lift Rule
rules.body: Only touchable or earned objects cast shadows. Bands, rails, trays and the ground stay flat.

dos: Do use palm green for every header band and its navigation bar, and rail green for the rail, with the same values in light and dark appearance.
Do put the Al-Sadu band only at a woven edge: header bottoms (30pt), the tray top (12pt), the celebration card (34pt) and rail covers (10pt).
Do show progress with shapes a pre-reader can count: eight diamonds per region, a starred gold stop, and the green seal on finished pages.
Do pair every child control with an SF Symbol and a short label, and keep child targets at 60pt or more.
Do use SF Rounded heavy for display and child-facing labels, and system text styles with a weight everywhere else.
Do keep paint pickers on plain system background so colours read true.
Do use leading and trailing (never left and right) and check every screen in Arabic RTL.
Do gate the large motion (mode slide, seal drop) on Reduce Motion.
donts: Don't give a region its own palette, header colour or ornament; the variety lives in the pages.
Don't add a second ornament or scatter Sadu pattern as a background texture.
Don't lay chrome, gradients or decoration over the scene art; the child's picture is the hero.
Don't give the green bars a separate dark-mode value; the bar and the header below it would split into two greens.
Don't recolour the Sadu band for dark mode or for a region; its colours are the weave's own.
Don't style the parental gate in the Rihla look; grown-up screens stay in the system sheet style.
Don't use text-only buttons in child-facing UI.
Don't use em-dashes in any user-facing copy.
